709704.t: From Proto-Indo-European *sop-lo- (“instrument”), an o-grade l-suffixed formation from *sep- (“to care for, honor, prepare”); see the related ἕπω (hépō, “I am busy”) for cognates. Not related to ἕπομαι (hépomai, “I follow”).

709780.t: Perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ergʰ- (“to mount”), whence also perhaps Hittite [script needed] (arkatta, “to mount sexually”).

709792.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₃ésth₁. Cognates include Latin os, Sanskrit अस्थि (ásthi), Old Armenian ոսկր (oskr), and Albanian asht.

709782.t: Of uncertain origin. Often explained as a derivative in *-iyo- from a participal form *s-o-to-s, beside alleged Proto-Indo-European *seto-s in ἐτάζω (etázō, “to examine, test”), although this account presents difficulties.

709781.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *hós, from Proto-Indo-European *Hyós, *Hyéh₂, *Hyód (“who, which”), from the relative stem *Hyo-, possibly from the anaphoric stem *(h₁)i-, *(h₁)e-.

709738.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ortʰwós, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃r̥dʰwós, from *h₃erdʰ- (“upright”). Cognate with Latin arduus, Sanskrit ऊर्ध्व (ūrdhvá).

709767.t: From Proto-Hellenic *órn-īk-s ~ *órn-īkʷʰ-, according to Beekes, from a feminine derivative ending in *-ih₂ of the oblique stem h₃er-n- of Proto-Indo-European *h₃érō.

709725.t: Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *wer- (“to watch, guard”). There may have been an intermediate form *ϝοράω (*worắō), from Proto-Hellenic *worā́ō.

709793.t: From ὅς (hós, “who, which”, relative pronoun) + τις (tĭs, “someone, anyone”, indefinite pronoun).

709716.t: Unknown. Not related to πέσσω (péssō, “to soften, ripen; to cook, dress, bake”).

709779.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₃órbʰos (“orphan”), from *h₃erbʰ- (“to change ownership”). Cognate with Latin orbus (“orphaned”), Sanskrit अर्भ (árbha, “small”), Old Armenian որբ (orb, “orphan”).

709762.t: From some derivation from Proto-Indo-European *h₃érō, whence also ὄρνις (órnis). Cognates include Old Armenian որոր (oror), Hittite 𒄩𒀀𒊏𒀸 (ḫāras), Proto-Slavic *orьlъ, and Old English earn (English erne).

709717.t: Seems to be a contraction of an original *ὀποσάρα (*oposára), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁epi (“on, at”) (whence ἐπί (epĭ́)) + *(s)h₁ósr̥, a variant of *(s)h₁ésō (“harvest season”), from *(s)h₁es- (“crop, harvest”); the exact formation *(s)h₁ósr̥ is found…

709768.t: Either from ὄρνυμι (órnumi, “I raise”), or possibly directly from a Proto-Indo-European *h₃eros; either way, derived from the root *h₃er- (“to rise, spring, stir”). Compare Sanskrit ऋ॒ष्व (ṛṣvá).

709756.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hοrmā́, with two plausible derivations: * From Proto-Indo-European *sor-meh₂- (“flow, stream”), from *ser- (“to flow, stream”), and thus cognate with Sanskrit सर्म (sárma, “going, running, flowing”), from the verb सरति (sarati, “to…

709769.t: From Proto-Hellenic *wórwos (whence Mycenaean Greek 𐀺𐀺 (wo-wo)), perhaps from a Proto-Indo-European *werw- (“to draw, mark out”), with cognates including Latin urvō (“to trace a boundary”).

709727.t: From Proto-Indo-European *werǵ- (“work”), formed similarly to ξόανον (xóănon, “statue, xoanon”); compare ἔργον (érgon, “work, deed”).

709796.t: Traditionally held to be related to ὀστέον (ostéon, “bone”) and ὄστρεον (óstreon, “oyster”). Beekes considers it more likely to be Pre-Greek, which does not exclude a relation to ὄστρεον (óstreon).

709753.t: Traditionally taken as an o-grade nominal formation from Proto-Indo-European *serḱ- (“to mend, fence”), whence also ἕρκος (hérkos, “fence”), i.e. "the bounds that one assumes" > "obligation, oath".

709774.t: A back-formation related to ὀρύσσω (orŭ́ssō, “to dig; to scrape”).

709710.t: From relative ὅς (hós) (or from its stem) + indefinite που (pou). Compare οὗ (hoû).

709719.t: From relative ὅς (hós) (or from its stem) + indefinite πως (pōs). Compare ὡς (hōs).

709728.t: From Proto-Indo-European *worǵéh₂, from the root *werǵ-; equivalent to ἔρδω (érdō) + -η (-ē). Compare Proto-Celtic *wergā.

709788.t: From Proto-Hellenic *yótsos, from earlier *Hyótyos, from Proto-Indo-European *Hyoti, adverb from *Hyós, whence ὅς (hós).

709745.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₃r̥dʰ-ro-, from *h₃erdʰ- (“to rise”). Cognate with ὀρθός (orthós), Latin ortus (“star's rise”), oriens (“sunrise”).

709709.t: From relative ὅς (hós) (or from its stem) + indefinite ποτέ (poté). Compare ὅτε (hóte).

709775.t: From Proto-Hellenic *orút͏̌t͏̌ō, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃rewk- (“to dig up, grub”). Cognate with Latin runcō.

709759.t: From Proto-Indo-European *sór-mos (compare Old Armenian որմ (orm, “wall, fence”)), from *ser- (“to bind”). Cognate with Ancient Greek εἴρω (eírō, “to tie, fasten”), Latin serō (“to bind”), Proto-Germanic *sarwą (“armour”).

709790.t: Of unclear origin. Connections with σπεῖρον (speîron, “wrapping cover”) and σπείρω (speírō, “to sow”) have been suggested, but this is impossible because "ὀ" is not a prothetic vowel.

709771.t: From an o-grade of ἐρέφω (eréphō, “to cover with a roof”) + -ος (-os).

709715.t: This verb's formation is similar to ἀρτάω (artáō), οὐτάω (outáō) and φοιτάω (phoitáō). It is commonly assumed that the verbal adjective ὀπτός (optós, “baked, roasted”) forms its basis.

709755.t: From ὁρμή (hormḗ, “start, impetus, rush, attack, effort”) + -άω (-áō, “verbal suffix”).

709707.t: From relative ὅς (hós) (or from its stem) + indefinite ποιός (poiós). Compare οἷος (hoîos).

709798.t: It is widely agreed that the initial syllable contains a zero grade s-stem from Proto-Indo-European *h₃ed-. Compare Ancient Greek ὄζω (ózō).

709758.t: ὅρμος (hórmos, “cord, necklace, collar”) + -ίσκος (-ĭ́skos, suffix forming diminutive nouns)
